title: Dr. DNA: Combating Silent Data Corruptions in Deep Learning using Distribution of Neuron Activations
problem: Silent data corruptions (SDCs) pose a stealthy and difficult-to-detect threat to DNN reliability in safety-critical applications as technology scales and hardware heterogeneity increases. These corruptions manifest elusive errors during inference that degrade model accuracy.
motivation: Deep neural networks are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications like autonomous driving and computer vision, where reliability is essential.
method: Dr. DNA extracts unique SDC signatures from the Distribution of Neuron Activations (DNA) to enable early-stage detection during inference. The approach identifies anomalous deviations in neuron activation patterns caused by silent data corruptions. Detected SDCs are mitigated to recover model performance with minimal computational overhead.
key_novelty: Using Distribution of Neuron Activations (DNA) as unique signatures to detect and mitigate silent data corruptions during DNN inference.
contributions: Novel SDC detection method based on neuron activation distribution signatures achieving 95% average detection rate
Integrated detection and mitigation framework enabling early error recovery in DNN inference
Comprehensive evaluation across 3 vision tasks, 5 datasets, and 10 models under 4 error models
Lightweight implementation with <1% memory overhead and <2.5% latency overhead

metrics.accuracy: 95% average SDC detection rate (100% for most cases, >90% across all cases), 20%-70% improvement over baselines

primary_theme: Silent data corruption detection in deep neural networks
